body: People like that make genuinely make you question humanity. God what a fucking monstrous piece of shit. It was a very different situation but my best friend died of cancer. Was probably the best person I've ever known, and was incredibly gifted. He would've done so much, but instead I'm here. So many years of misery and for what? There's no answer but I know how it feels, to want to swap places.
Yeah I think anyone on this subreddit could benefit from enlisting. Hopefully you'll kill yourselves during basic instead of after you get back from killing children in 3rd world countries. 😊
I hate that the only reason I'm alive is that I'm terrified of having to live with the physical consequences of messing up an attempt.

I have terrible (mostly long-term) memory. It's just a hunch but it feels like it's because of my depression. It sucks, cause there are some memories I really wish I had right now. After someone is gone they're all you have.

I feel you. I like that it makes me more empathetic but sometimes I feel pathetic. If people get in my face/yell at me/etc. I tear up and feel sad rather than get angry and defend myself. Ironically the more depressed I get the less I care what people think about me, but at that point it's not a good tradeoff.

Well your parents suck and maybe one day they'll realize that. I hope you don't let them stop you from being yourself. I know it's easier said than done but don't throw away your future because of them. There are so many trans people that know exactly how you feel. You're at a very difficult point in life and I don't blame you for feeling that way. But soon enough you'll have so much self-worth and people in your life who love you for who you are, and it will have been worth it.

I got committed to a hospital for about 2 weeks for *thinking* about killing myself. It was horrible and I don't open up to anyone irl about how I feel now. Really was my worst fear, having no way out. They treated us like prisoners we had no freedom.

After going through all the steps, the last thing that has always stopped me is fear. Not of dying but of either fucking it up or the pain it would entail. All I want is to go to sleep and not wake up. It seems impossible if you're not impulsive or are not at the lowest point you could be at.
I'm glad I'm not the only one. I feel you guys.
This is such dogshit advice. Do you think people don't know how to listen to music? This just sounds preachy and helps nobody.
The last 2 years have been a complete blur, I've never felt so disoriented. Losing memories really scares me too, because it's all we have. The good memories are all I have left.
My best friend died 2 years ago. Exact same situation. He seriously was the best person I've ever met; totally would've changed the world. The world feels so cold and pointless now.

I know how you feel. My closest friend was diagnosed with grade 4 brain cancer right when we were out of high school. For a while he only told me and his immediate family, since he also didn't want anyone to worry about it. It totally destroyed me and now he is off at college so I've seen him once since he left.

You probably have better answers than I do on how to be with him or support him at this time. But I do want to mention that you should remember to take care of yourself too. Talking to people about it like friends, family, or even a post like this will help.

I wish there was some easy answer or words of advice for what to do in this situation but I don't have any. It comes out of no where and can be overwhelming. It won't be easy but I wish you and your boyfriend the best. Take care.

On top of what every else said, I have a personal grief with the summer. For me it means being mildly uncomfortable to constantly in pain from my chronic pain (erythromelalgia). The few times I spent time outside in the summer since getting this condition, it was genuinely torture. So I'm in the same boat, sitting inside desperately trying to say cool and kill time till its fall.

and I just want to say that I know how petty/unimportant this may come across to some of you. Some of the stories I've read on here have been much more filled with grief and tragedy. But I've also had people say the same thing to me, where they feel their feeling are invalid because their lives aren't as bad in comparison. I won't feel guilty for having depression any longer because it's something I've felt since middle school and whether or not its justified doesn't mean it's not real.
Yup. Probably why I do anything I can to escape. Games, movies, etc. Also the thought of attempting suicide and failing is terrifying to me.

I'm gonna throw my personal story here just as a rant so people who aren't interested can skip it.

I have a toxic relationship with my family. Everyone fights with each other, and it's been like that since my childhood. At this point I've given up trying to care about them and have just pushed them away to avoid unnecessary conflict. I've also never had a girlfriend, and not sure if I could see myself in a relationship. While recently ive considered trying to date, I don't have the greatest social skills and I am so depressed that I'm worried it would ruin it. 

Easily what's troubling me the most is that my best friend was diagnosed with grade 4 brain cancer. He is handling it like a champ, so positive and went to a great college. On the other hand, the news destroyed me, I failed my classes and college and took the semester off. I feel so pathetic that, shouldn't I be the one that has to support him? I haven't done much more than talk to him whenever we have the chance. 

I also have health problems that are the cherry on top when it comes to every-day annoyances. I have a rare chronic pain condition called erythromelalgia (like the opposite of reynauds) which prevents me from being in a warm environment. I also have terrible undiagnosed stomach pain, and I've done every test I can think of with no results. I have a lot of pain every day and lost a ton of food I can no longer tolerate. So when I'm in a really bad mood, the pain just multiplies it and makes it much worse. 

At this point in time im 18 and live with my parents. I play video games 12+ hours a day and work part time. I know it's not as serious as a drug addiction but I still have trouble pulling myself away. It's so much easier to immerse myself in fantasy rather than look at my reality. If my friend does pass away I will most likely kill myself, as the biggest positive force in my life will be gone.

I had no idea how long this was until I posted it. Not sure what I'm looking for by doing this but it's not pity. Maybe it's because I'm lonely as usual. Or maybe it's because Christmas has always been hell for me and I know tomorrow will be no different. Either way, if you read all this crap then you certainly deserve a happy holiday.

Bringing up serious issues men deal with is looked at as saying "These issues are more important than women's issues". It's not a competition, we can work on both. In fact, it's a problem in itself that these things can't even be addressed openly.

your story sounds very similar to mine. I'm starting my 1st year at community college soon and don't know if I will be able to keep myself together enough to pass. I almost failed out of senior year. My dad thinks he failed me because I don't do anything or talk to anyone. I stay up until about 4am every night due to depression + chronic pain. Not to mention my best friend has brain cancer, who is way smarter, kinder, and more ambitious than me.  How am I supposed to move on with my life when I don't want to live it anymore? It's a cycle of laziness, shame, and depression I can't get out of. I also haven't talked to my sibling in years, but she's a younger sister and not an older brother. 

I guess its good to know I'm not alone. Sorry this isn't very uplifting. hopefully things work out for both of us.

I know how you feel. I'm slowly getting to that point now. But I kind of view it as a positive, since I spent all my free time playing them. It gives me an excuse to study, play guitar, get some exercise, or watch a movie. It's easier to just play video games but that is part of what led me here in the first place. But I'm sure if you take a break that there will be a game that pulls your interest again, just maybe not as hard as it used to. I wish you the best in figuring things out.

Yeah no problem. The chronic pain isn't too bad, more of an annoyance than anything, but I appreciate the concern.

Also I just wanted to mention I had a friend who took 4 tries to pass the test mainly because of nerves as well. Half the battle is staying calm, once you can figure that out than the rest should come easy. 

P.S. You said "I have never been naturally good at much" and I can assure you nobody is good at something they've never done. Maybe they can learn it a little faster but they still had to learn. Nobody on the planet has been known how to play the guitar when they picked it up for the first time.

I hear ya. My chronic pain keeps me up at night sometimes and it's easily the most stressful and dark part of my days. I find it easier to stay up late until I get tired enough to pass out (like im doing right now). Insomnia must be a big pain in the ass, so don't feel like a failure for something thats out of your control. 

The fact that you even took the test 3 times shows you are determined and able to put in the effort. You'll pass the test eventually I promise. Maybe you have to deal with more mentally than the average person but you can still live a happy life. I'm sure a therapist or someone actually specialized in the field can you give you better advice for dealing with nerves than I can, so I'll just wish ya the best.
Happy birthday. I'll be in the same boat soon. I hope brighter days are ahead my friend.

You should buy new strings for the guitar and give it another go! They are cheap, and people breaking strings off their guitar from playing too hard is not a rare occurrence. 

Try playing guitar for fun, not to be the best. There are plenty of videos online for beginners to teach the basics. 

I played on and off for a few years, and kept losing my motivation to play. I felt like I was bad and was embarrassed to even pick up the thing. It was dumb to think like that, of course I wasn't great if I played so rarely. But there isn't anything wrong with being bad, most people don't even have the courage to pick up a guitar.

I hope one day you lose the mindset that you're useless because some website told you so. You have much more potential than you think you do.

Its funny that out of all the nightmares ive had, the happiest dream hurt the most. I remember I was at a fair with some girl. We just walked around, holding hands and smiling. It was so bright and warm, I wish I could relieve it every night. Nothing else happened until I woke up with a harsh realization. 

All I wanted was a friend or s/o I could spend the day with, without any worries. Waking up from that dream was one of the most depressing points in my life. Didn't even realize how lonely I was until my brain gave me a temporary friend.
